newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong silent on Korean defections.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong silent on Korean defections.

text.p: Hong Kong authorities on Sunday declined to comment on media reports that two more North Koreans had fled to the British territory, where 17 other escapees sought refuge last week.

"We do not make any comment on such reports," a government spokesman said by telephone, referring to a report carried by South Korea's Yonhap News Agency on Sunday which said two North Koreans had fled to Hong Kong.

Last week, 17 other escapees -- 16 members of one family and a security guard -- sought refuge in Hong Kong in the biggest mass defection from the communist nation since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War and were waiting for asylum in South Korea.
Officials from Hong Kong's Immigration Department, Security Branch and the South Korean consulate were not immediately available for comment.

Yonhap quoted a Hong Kong source as identifying the two latest escapees as Yu Bong-nam, a member of the North Korean Public Security Ministry, and Chon Hak-chol who it described as a North Korean intelligence agent.
However the Korea Broadcasting System said Chon was a North Korean student, not an intelligence agent.
Yonhap said the latest two escapees brought to 35 the total number of North Koreans who have fled to Hong Kong to seek asylum in South Korea since 1993.
The two Koreas have been technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean War.
